events.title: Rob McWilliams Band at The Jazz Sessions
events.description: Rob McWilliams Band Professor Rob McWilliams has led an interesting life. A musician and composer, playing trumpet, flugelhorn and piano, he has been part of the jazz scene for many years, originally playing professionally in Melbourne with artists such as Wilbur Wilde and Paul Grabowsky. His studies and high level of musicianship led him to the USA where he took up the post of Professor of Music at the University of Wisconsin, Oshkosh and ended up as Head of Music there for several years. As a teacher he has presented at major music conferences in Japan, Hong Kong, the UK, Singapore, Europe, China and Australia and is a published author. As a musician he has performed with many jazz greats including Nat Adderley, Vincent Herring, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Eddie Daniels, Ed Shaughnessy and Dale Barlow – a resume that is the envy of many an Australian jazz musician! A talented musician, composer and arranger, Rob has had many opportunities over the years to create and perform his music to audiences all over the world. Now living back in Australia, he works for Yamaha Music conducting music workshops around Australia as well as teaching at the Jazz Music Institute in Brisbane, conducting, composing, arranging music and performing regularly around Australia either as a side man or with his own jazz ensemble. Though he is a Professor with an incredible and impressive Curriculum Vitae, he is a warm and down-to-earth performer with a genuine connection to the audience, bringing the music alive. This masterful musician in now bringing his music to the Sunshine Coast, performing with his band at The Jazz Sessions at The Presynct on Thurs 17th Sep. Joined on this gig by a stellar line-up of local Brisbane & Sunshine Coast musicians, they have come together to perform unique interpretations of jazz standards and some of Rob’s original compositions. Be prepared for an evening of sophistication, smooth jazz and world-class musicianship. VENUE & EVENT DETAILS 📅 Thursday 17th September 📍The Presynct, Upstairs- 15 Ann St, Nambour ⏰ Doors 6:00pm | Event 6:30pm -9:00pm 🚗 Parking available behind the Venue 🎟 Tickets $25-$45 🩴 NO Thongs Permitted 🚱 NO Outside Drink bottles If you’re looking for a unique concert experience, look no further than The Jazz Sessions at The Presynct. This hidden gem offers intimate shows for listeners in a beautifully curated venue. These are listening concerts where people can come together to enjoy live music in a true jazz club experience. We ask that talking is kept to a quiet whisper as audience members are actively listening to and connecting with the artists in a relaxed and comfortable setting. These concerts give guests the opportunity to experience exceptional musicianship in an intimate setting.

events.title: Body Type
events.location: Mapleton Public House, Mapleton · Nambour + Hinterland
events.description: Over the past decade, Body Type have established themselves as one of Australia’s most acclaimed and compelling bands. Since forming in Sydney in 2016, they have released two celebrated albums, earned an Australian Music Prize nomination, toured extensively throughout Australia, Europe and the UK, and shared stages with Foo Fighters, Fontaines D.C., Pixies, Big Thief, Warpaint, Sleater-Kinney and Cate Le Bon. Now, the four-piece return with Tally, their third album and most ambitious work to date. Marking the band’s tenth anniversary, Tally captures a group taking stock, embracing change and pushing their sound into bold new territory while retaining the wit, charm and sharp observations that have become their trademark. Recorded in Los Angeles with acclaimed producer Stella Mozgawa (Warpaint, Courtney Barnett), Tally draws inspiration from a wide range of sources: the work of artist Louise Bourgeois, misty drives through the Hollywood Hills, 10 years of history as a band. The album transforms the everyday into something surreal, witty and profound while exploring love, friendship, insecurity and the strange beauty hidden within ordinary life.

events.description: BATS THEATRE COMPANY PROUDLY PRESENTS - INSPECTOR DRAKE AND THE BLACK WIDOW Imagine if Fawlty Towers meets a murder mystery. That is, essentially, Inspector Drake and the Black Widow. A classic English farce featuring a cross between ‘Inspector Clouseau’ and ‘And Then There Were None’ will have you laughing out loud and forgetting about the outside world. A dead body is found, whilst dusting at 3am, which sets up a play that is an amusing parody of the whodunnit genre, that’s packed with lots of visual gags, subtle adult innuendo, all topped with a touch of cross-dressing. The plot, set in the 1920s , has Sergeant Plod send for the infamous Inspector Drake to help solve the murder of John Johnson who has been stabbed in the back whilst wearing his wife’s dress. The two are thwarted by a series of women who look suspiciously alike, with triplets born two months apart, a missing semi-tropical spider and a lustful widow. Just a few of the obstacles facing Inspector Drake. Imagine Basil Fawlty playing Inspector Clouseau playing Inspector Drake? What can possibly go wrong? From the Team at BATS Theatre, that brought you ‘Sex Please, We’re Sixty’. events.title: Functional Circuit Training
events.location: Buderim War Memorial Hall - CWA Room upstairs, 1 Main Street
events.description: Healthy Sunshine Coast is excited to offer Functional Circuit Training sessions with Gaye Becker from Just 4 Your Fitness. Functional training is a term used to describe exercise that helps you perform activities in everyday life more easily. These exercises typically use the whole body - definitely multiple muscles - and emphasise core strength and stability. By mirroring the movements of your daily life, like squatting, reaching or even carrying a heavy object, building functional strength can help increase your quality of life and reduce your risk of injury. Every Wednesday CWA room, upstairs at the Buderim War Memorial Hall Provider: Gaye Becker - 0450 870 332 bodyfit.63@gmail.com Bookings: Required - either call or email Gaye. Cost: only $10 general fee or $5 health care/pensioner card Details: Look on Council’s website and search for ‘Healthy Sunshine Coast’, then locate ‘Healthy Sunshine Coast Activities’ and click on the box below.
